title: Pipkin and the Shape Muddle
markdown:
In Toby the bridge maker’s cozy workshop, soft lamplight made wood shavings sparkle. Toby hummed a gentle tune, and Pipkin the hamster watched, wishing he could help.

The shape shelf was a wobbly tumbling mess. Round circles rolled with steady squares, and pointy triangles peeked from the jumble. “Oh, Pipkin,” Toby whispered, “how will we find the round wheels or the square windows when it’s such a muddle?” Pipkin nudged a circle, but it bumped a triangle, which bumped a square. Everything wobbled more.

Auntie Flo put her head round the door, left a cup of warm milk on the bench, and did not fuss. The workshop kept its hush.

Then Pipkin’s paw nudged a pile of shapes, and as he nudged gently, the round circles rolled together. The flat squares settled with a quiet thump. The pointy triangles gathered like little tents. Pipkin paused, bright eyes wide. He nudged a circle, and it rolled back to its friends. He pushed a square, and it stayed nestled beside another.

“Well, I never,” Toby murmured, leaning closer. “Look, Pipkin. When you move them so gently, the circles roll together, the squares sit so steady, and the triangles find their pointy companions.” He picked up a round circle. “See how it loves to roll?” He picked up a flat square. “And this one likes to stay still and neat.” Pipkin squeaked with delight. He understood. The shapes were different, and liked to stay with their own kind.

Toby smiled, a warm soft smile. “If we help them find their friends and sort them by their shape, the shelf will be tidy again.” Carefully, Toby placed all the round circles in one spot. Pipkin nudged all the steady squares together. Toby gathered the pointy triangles. Soon the shelf was a calm pattern of circles, squares, and triangles, all in their happy places.

“You see, Pipkin,” Toby said softly, as moonlight gleamed, “when we put things that are alike together, it’s easier to find what we need. Like putting all your sleepy thoughts together for sweet dreams.” Pipkin yawned a tiny soft yawn. He snuggled deep into Toby’s warm gentle paw. The workshop felt peaceful, pale moonlight and Toby’s quiet hum. Auntie Flo’s milk steamed, forgotten and kind. And soon Toby’s soft lullaby lulled Pipkin, and Toby too, into a warm quiet wonderful slumber. Everything was just right.
characters: Pipkin (a hamster), Toby (a bridge maker), Flo (an auntie)
